description: Mean, median, mode, quartiles and standard deviation.

faqs.a: Quartiles use linear interpolation between closest ranks (the same method as NumPy's default). Other tools may differ slightly in the quartile method they use.
Both are shown. Population variance divides by n (the data is everything); sample variance divides by n−1 (the data is a sample of something bigger).
faqs.q: Population vs sample — which do I need?

faqs.a: The mode is the most frequent value. If every value appears the same number of times, the tool reports that there is no mode instead of inventing one.
faqs.q: What is the mode when all values are unique?

howto: Paste or type numbers separated by commas, spaces or new lines.
Read n, sum, min, max, range, mean, median and mode(s).
Compare population and sample variance/standard deviation, plus Q1, Q3 and IQR.
